name: PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk

frontmatter.title: Baramulti Suksessarana: restated earnings, a reserve-capped NAV and the dividends already paid
frontmatter.summary: This revision answers the QC's first round. We restate FY2025 depreciation from the company's own EBITDA margin, cap the life-of-mine DCF at the measured resource, align FY2026 fuel cost with the through-cycle price used for revenue, and hold operating cost at the first-half actual. The two dividends paid after the 30 June balance sheet are deducted in the bridge, and the forward dividend is the residual final tranche.
thesis: We hold HOLD with a Rp4,936 target and a 3.3% total return against the Rp5,000 price; this revision is an accounting and bridge correction, not a new price forecast.
The FATAL is fixed — the 23.3% FY2025 EBITDA margin in [S16] implies US$61.7m of depreciation, so FY2025 EBITDA is US$164.0m and the forecast adds the full charge back to cash flow [S16].
The life-of-mine DCF is the primary method at 65% and gives Rp4,431; it discounts exactly the 147 Mt measured resource and stops when the stock is mined [S8].

The bridge deducts the FY2025 final and FY2026 interim dividends already paid after the balance sheet — US$70.0m and US$60.0m — and the next-twelve-month dividend is the residual final tranche [S11][S7].
The bull is disclosed as incomplete on the upside, the bear prices conversion failure at the 32.3 Mt proved reserve, and the unconfirmed contract royalty is the one input we cannot source [S16].

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and the FY2027 volume plan
RKAB 2027 production approval (national quota and BSSR volume)
FY2026 annual report: reserve/resource restatement and contract-rate confirmation

blocks.text: We hold **HOLD** on PT Baramulti Suksessarana Tbk (BSSR) with a twelve-month target of **Rp4,936**, a total return of **3.3%** against the Rp5,000 price [S0]. BSSR mines thermal coal from concessions in South and East Kalimantan through its operating subsidiary PT Antang Gunung Meratus and its own blocks, and sells most of its output to export buyers [S8][S16].

**What changed and why.** This is a revision after the QC's first round, and the changes are technical rather than a new view on coal. First, the earnings restatement stands: the data pack carries a residual depreciation charge, while the company's own reported EBITDA margin implies US$61.7m of depreciation in FY2025 [S16], which lifts FY2025 EBITDA to US$164.0m and adds the full charge back to cash flow. Second, the bridge now deducts the two dividends that left the company after the 30 June 2026 balance sheet: the FY2025 final of US$70.0m approved on 15 June and paid on 8 July, which was already a liability at the balance-sheet date, and the FY2026 interim of US$60.0m paid on 9 October [S11][S7]. Net cash to equity was therefore overstated by the first and the forward dividend excludes the second. Third, we align the cost side with the revenue side: FY2026 fuel is priced at the through-cycle brent that prices the coal marker, not at the war print, and operating cost is held at the first-half actual ratio [S2][S0]. The primary DCF gives Rp4,431 and the EV/EBITDA cross-check gives Rp5,819 at 5.3x; blended at 65% / 35%, the target is Rp4,936 [model].

**The base case is the most likely path.** We anchor volume on the company's 17.0 Mt FY2026 production target converted to sales at the last actual sales ratio, and on a realisation that prices the year at the desk's through-cycle marker rather than its war print, so FY2026 revenue is US$729.3m and EBITDA US$185.0m [S16][S0]. That revenue is essentially twice the first-half actual of US$361.1m [S2]; the full-year marker in the desk deck is deliberately not carried because it would imply a second-half price above today's spot [S0]. On cost we now carry the first half's own run-rate rather than the FY2025 ratio: the half earned a 37.4% gross margin and a US$79.7m operating profit, and its dollar operating expense was below the FY2025 level [S2][S0]. FY2026 net profit is US$98.3m. The simple first-half annualisation overstates the full year because the first half carried the war print and the second half does not; we carry the reversion in the base and the war print in the bull.

**What the market prices and what we think differ on method.** The life DCF discounts the resource at through-cycle prices and puts the shares close to fair value; the earnings multiple capitalises one year at the last actual's price and sits 31.3% above it [model][S0]. We keep the DCF dominant at 65% and hold the multiple at 35%; that blend produces the -1.3% gap to the target, and the next-twelve-month dividend of Rp232 — the residual final tranche after the October interim — supplies the rest of the total return [model][S7].

Two things move the value. The first is the coal marker: Newcastle averaged US$108/t in the last actual and the desk carries it to US$105/t long run [S0]. The second is the royalty: the operating company mines under a coal contract of work [S19], but the contract rate is not in the archive, so it is an explicit unconfirmed rate rather than a schedule read [S0][S19]. We flag it rather than bury it.

Coal miners are price-takers whose equity is a leveraged call on the marker and the state take. In
Indonesia the fiscal wedge between the mine gate and the sale is set by the licence and the royalty
schedule attached to it, so two otherwise identical pits hand very different shares of the same tonne
to the government. Investors in the sector trade the dividend and the reserve life as much as the
earnings.

BSSR is a thermal-coal producer. It operates through its wholly owned subsidiary PT Antang Gunung Meratus in South Kalimantan and through its own blocks in East Kalimantan, and it markets coal to China, India, Japan, Taiwan, the Philippines, Hong Kong, South Korea and Thailand as well as domestically [S8]. The company was incorporated in 1990, is headquartered in Jakarta and is controlled by PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang with a very small free float [S0].

The product is a low-calorie thermal coal sold largely to export buyers. In the first half of 2026, export sales were 82.0% of total sales, up from about seven in ten a year earlier [S2]. The FY2025 marketing mix put Indonesia at roughly three-tenths of volume, with China and India the two largest export destinations [S16]. The revenue model is simple and cyclical: tonnes times the realised price, with the realised price a deep discount to the high-grade export marker because the coal is lower in calorific value [S8][S16].

Strategy is price defence and reserve conversion rather than growth. Management deliberately cut output in FY2025, production falling to 17.8 Mt from 21.4 Mt in FY2024 [S16][S9], and said the decision protected margin; the first half of 2026 was stronger as a consequence [S16][S2]. In parallel the company is drilling to convert its resource base into reserves, running a modest exploration budget on its East Kalimantan blocks in Kutai Kartanegara, and it has said it is looking at new coal assets [S12][S16]. The exploration effort matters more than its size suggests: with proved reserves thin relative to the annual plan rate, the mine's life depends on converting the wider resource base, so drilling results are a first-order input to the value rather than a distant option [S16][S12].

BSSR is a mid-tier producer, not a leader. Its scale is a fraction of the large Indonesian coal names and its product sits in the lower-grade segment, where the buyer set is narrower and the price is more elastic [S8][S10]. It carries no listed subsidiaries beyond its operating company, so the equity is a clean read on one mining business rather than a holding-company puzzle [S8]. The controlling shareholder structure means the shares are effectively a minority claim on a family- and strategically-controlled asset, which shapes both the liquidity and the capital-return decisions [S0].

Indonesian thermal coal is a large, policy-managed export industry. National coal export value rose year on year over the first nine months even as export tonnage fell, because prices rose while volumes dropped [S10]. The government manages supply through the annual RKAB production approval and, since 2025, through an administered reference price (HBA) that acts as a floor for export pricing [S16][S10]. Indonesia is reported to be allowing a higher national production quota after a relaxation of the RKAB [S10]. The policy tilt matters for BSSR twice: a higher national quota loosens the supply discipline that supports price, and the administered HBA floor sets the export pricing reference and the DMO cap [S10][S0]. The royalty, though, keys off the contract rather than the HBA band, for the licence reason set out below.

The driver that prices this name is the Newcastle marker carried in the desk coal deck at US$108/t for the last actual and US$105/t long run [S0]. The reviewed Indonesian grade indices that would price BSSR's lower-calorie product more precisely (ICI-4 and ICI-3) are marked needs_source in the deck, so we price off the reviewed Newcastle series and calibrate the discount on our own actuals; the HBA series (US$118/t for FY2026) is used only for the royalty band and the DMO cap [S0]. The DMO cap for power-sector coal is a standing regulatory ceiling of US$70.0/t per tonne, which does not bind at our realised price [S0].

Regulation is the swing factor, and the licence class here is sourced. BSSR's operating company mines under a **coal contract of work** — the *Perjanjian Karya Pengusahaan Pertambangan Batu bara*, the pre-2009 generation of Indonesian coal contracts — and AGM is described in the Indonesian press in exactly those terms: a "perusahaan pemegang kontrak Perjanjian Karya Pengusahaan Pertambangan Batu bara" [S19]. That settles the class question earlier drafts carried open, and it sets the mechanism: a contract of work's royalty and PNBP follow the individual contract until its term ends, so the deck maps the class to a contract-specific rate and the banded calorie-by-HBA open-pit schedules do not govern it [S0][S19]. Because the contract rate itself is not in the archive, the rate is an explicit unconfirmed parameter rather than a schedule read: we carry 14.8% of revenue, US$107.6m in FY2026 [S0]. We searched the archived record in full for a royalty or PNBP line and found none, so the base sits between the two schedule values that are reachable at our HBA path — the ex-contract IUPK continuation band and the plain-IUP mid-calorie band — and the reader sees the sensitivity rather than a hidden assumption [S0][S21]. The house deck's own ex-contract-holder continuation list does not include BSSR or AGM, which is why we do not carry the ex-contract band as the base; the contract rate is the single largest unconfirmed input in this report [S0].

The moat is thin. BSSR has no cost-curve leadership that we can source, its product sits in the lower-grade segment, and its position in China and India is that of a swing supplier to buyers who can substitute other tonnes [S16][S10]. The five forces are unfavourable on rivalry and buyer power and only modestly favourable on the regulatory barrier to entry the licence confers. On share, BSSR is a mid-tier producer: its annual tonnage is a small fraction of what the large Indonesian houses ship, so it is a price-taker with no ability to set the marker it is paid against [S8][S10]. External influences the model carries are the coal marker itself, the rupiah path and Indonesian policy — the administered reference price, the annual quota and the royalty schedule [S0][S10].

The seaborne thermal coal market clears on the marginal tonne from Indonesia and Australia, so each
grade trades at a discount to the high-grade marker that widens when demand softens and narrows when
it tightens. Indonesian producers additionally carry a policy layer (quotas, an administered floor
price, domestic-market obligations) that other origins do not.

Revenue fell from US$1,029.0m in FY2022 to US$703.8m in FY2025 as prices came off the 2022 peak and the company cut volumes [S0][S16]. FY2025 cost of revenue was US$495.2m and gross profit US$208.6m, an EBITDA of US$164.0m at a margin of 23.3% [S0][S16]. That margin is the fixed point of this revision: at US$703.8m of revenue it implies US$164.0m of EBITDA against reported EBIT of US$102.3m, hence US$61.7m of depreciation [S16][S0]. The roll-forward corroborates it independently: opening property, plant and equipment of US$143.9m plus capex of US$33.9m less closing US$117.0m is the same order of charge [S0]. No archived source carries a depreciation line — the FY2025 audited accounts are not in the archive and the company site is unreachable — so the margin-implied figure is the best available and is disclosed as computed [S0][S16].

Our forecast holds the company's plan rate of 16.8 Mt of sales, the 17.0 Mt FY2026 production target converted at the last actual sales ratio, and the calibrated realisation of 31.8%, so FY2026 revenue is US$729.3m and EBITDA US$185.0m [S16][S2]. Revenue is twice the first-half actual of US$361.1m [S2] — we anchor the year to the first half and to the desk's through-cycle marker rather than its full-year war print, which implies a second-half price above today's spot [S0]. The cash cost is 20.1 per tonne in the first forecast year and holds at that level through the horizon: the FY2026 fuel pass-through is set against the through-cycle brent marker, not the war print, so a cost line inflated by a price we do not carry on the revenue side does not enter the year [S0][S16]. Royalty at our stated base rate is US$107.6m in the first forecast year [S0][S16]. SG&A runs at 13.8% of sales, the first-half 2026 actual US$100.6m on our revenue, rather than the FY2025 ratio [S2][S0].

The first half of 2026 is the live check on those costs, and it cuts in our favour. It earned a 37.4% gross margin and a US$79.7m operating profit on US$361.1m of revenue [S2]. We carry that operating-cost run-rate, but we still price the year at the desk's through-cycle marker rather than its full-year war print, so our FY2026 net profit of US$98.3m sits below a simple first-half annualisation; the first half alone was US$63.0m [S2][S16]. That gap is the deliberate price anchor and the main upside case, not a hidden cost buffer: the bull scenario carries the war print and its value lift is shown with the scenarios [S0].

Working capital is a drag held at the last actual: operating working capital was US$71.4m [S0], and we carry 10.1% of revenue rather than a three-year average that would book a release. Capex is small: the FY2026 budget is US$26.3m [S16], about 1.6 per tonne. The balance sheet is conservative: net debt at the FY2025 year-end was US$-43.0m against EBITDA of US$164.0m, with cash of US$44.2m and debt of US$1.3m [S0].

**Earnings-quality flags.** First, **payout above earnings, but cash-covered**: the FY2025 payout of 148.8% — US$125.0m declared against parent profit of US$84.0m [S11] — is a policy choice, and the pack's own operating cash flow less capex exceeded the declared dividend in FY2025 [S0]. The board has repeated it: the FY2026 interim of US$60.0m is close to all of first-half net profit of US$63.0m [S7][S2]. The dividend is funded from cash; the question is how long a thin reserve base can sustain it, not whether last year's was covered. Second, **reserve cover is thin and the two statements conflict**: [S16] dates 32.3 Mt of proved reserves at 31 December 2025 [S16], while [S8] states 62.6 Mt of *mineable* proved reserves and a 147 Mt measured resource with no as-of date and no basis statement [S8]. We present both as undated or conflicting rather than forcing a chronology the sources do not support, and we use the measured resource only as the DCF's depleting stock, never more. Third, **depreciation is now restated, not a flag**: the US$61.7m charge above replaces the pack's residual, and the forecast holds it at 3.5 per tonne so cash flow carries the full add-back [S16][S0]. Cash conversion is clean: the model's FY2025 free cash flow of US$87.0m understates the pack's cash generation because it charges a working-capital build, but the underlying earnings were cash-backed [S0]. No manipulation-class flag was found: the FY2024 accounts carried an unqualified opinion [S9], there is no special-notation or monitoring-board status in the record we hold, and no related-party flow of note appears in any archived source — sales to, purchases from and loans to affiliates are not disaggregated in the record we hold, so we cannot quantify a related-party share of revenue and say so rather than assume zero [S8][S9][S16].

We value BSSR with the house commodity-producer method set: a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices as the primary method, cross-checked against an EV/EBITDA multiple [config]. This is the right frame for a price-taking producer because spot earnings and current-year multiples are procyclical: a low multiple on a peak year is not value, and a high one on a trough year is not expensiveness.

The cost of capital is built from the macro deck: a risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market equity premium of 4.2%, an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, an unlevered beta of 0.80 (the COAL default) and a tax rate of 22.0%, giving a cost of equity of 10.3% and a WACC of 10.3% [S0]. BSSR carries effectively no net debt, so the WACC is the cost of equity [S0].

The primary DCF gives Rp4,431 per share at a 65% weight and an enterprise value of US$663.1m [model]. It takes no terminal value (0.0%) and it discounts exactly the 147 Mt measured resource, fed into the template as a depleting stock: the mine runs at the plan rate until the stock is exhausted and then stops [S8][model]. The reserve ladder is disclosed around it. The bear schedules only the 32.3 Mt proved reserve at 31 December 2025 and is worth Rp2,425; the base carries the 147 Mt measured resource and is worth Rp5,192; the 62.6 Mt mineable-proved statement of [S8] sits between the two and is disclosed rather than used as a third anchor [S16][S8]. Nothing beyond the measured resource is capitalised.

The EV/EBITDA cross-check gives Rp5,819 at 5.3x, 31.3% above the primary [model]. We do not treat that as a reason to chase the shares, and we decompose the gap. It applies the COAL peer median to one year at the last actual's US$108/t benchmark rather than the asset's life, so it carries no forecast fade and no reserve-life risk [model][S0]; the same multiple on the restated EBITDA is, however, a fair statement of what a buyer pays for a year of this cash flow today. The target blends the two at 65% / 35%.

The equity bridge starts from the last disclosed balance sheet and must be walked forward for the dividend declarations it predates. At 30 June 2026 the company's net cash is before two post-balance-sheet payments: the FY2025 final dividend of US$70.0m declared at the June RUPST and paid in July, which was a current liability at the balance-sheet date, and the FY2026 interim of US$60.0m declared in September and paid in October [S11][S7]. Both are carried as cash outflows in the bridge, so the equity value the DCF produces is net of the money that has already left the company; the FY2025 final is a deduction from net cash, not a double count against the asset value, because the DCF's base is the enterprise, not the dividend stream [model][S11][S7].

We no longer capitalise the dividend as a valuation leg. At the base payout the next-twelve-month dividend is Rp232, a 4.6% yield at the current price [model], and the pack's trailing dividend yield is higher still [S0]. That figure is the residual final tranche of the FY2026 declaration — what remains of the payout year after the October interim — not a cut in policy, and the model's dividend line for FY2026 is that residual because the interim is already paid and bridged [model][S7]. A no-depletion perpetuity at a peer cap rate was the defect the red team identified, and a declining-dividend treatment would be a second guess on top of an unconfirmed reserve life; the dividend stays in the total return, not in the target [model]. That leaves the DCF and the multiple as the two methods, and the dividend as a prose cross-check.

What today's price implies: a reverse DCF on the marker price needs a factor of 1.1, about US$124/t, which is close to our through-cycle assumption [model]. In other words the shares are roughly fairly valued on a life-of-mine view; the gap to our target comes from the multiple cross-check, not from a cycle call. Today's Rp5,000 buys a 7.3x forward P/E and a 4.6% dividend yield at our numbers [model].

Two lines the card's output contract asks for, so the reader can see how much of the rating is cycle position rather than the asset. **NAV at spot**: the primary is the through-cycle NAV at US$105/t; marking the same tonnes at today's spot marker (US$150/t) is a different number and the sensitivity table carries that axis [model][S0]. **Cost-curve quartile**: a house read, not a sourced fact — we cannot source a cost curve for this name and say so — on the realised price and the cash cost the wider Indonesian peer set carries, BSSR reads as a mid-cost, lower-middle-quartile thermal producer with no cost-curve leadership we can evidence. **Net debt against trough EBITDA**: at the last actual the company carried net cash — US$-43.0m against EBITDA of US$164.0m — so net-debt/trough-EBITDA is negative however deep the trough: the balance sheet is a buffer, not a lever [S0].

The biggest risk is the one number we still cannot read: the **contract royalty rate**. The licence class is sourced — AGM mines under a coal contract of work [S19] — so the state take follows the individual contract and the deck's contract-of-work schedule is contract-specific rather than the banded IUPK/IUP tables [S0][S19]; but the rate the contract sets is not in the archive, and a full-text search of every registered source finds no royalty or PNBP line. It is therefore an unconfirmed parameter at 14.8% of revenue at our HBA path, and we carry that rate in every scenario rather than using the royalty as a one-way bull shock. The scalar risk is the width of the reachable schedule values around it. The first thing to confirm from the FY2026 annual report is the contract rate. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high.

Other risks. **Coal price**: the marker averaged US$108/t in the last actual against a spot of US$150/t, and the deck expects mean reversion to US$105/t; a war premium that fades early hits a low-calorie seller first [S0][S16]. Likelihood: high. Impact: high. **Volume and market access**: BSSR is a swing supplier to China and India, and Indonesian quota policy has moved sharply in both directions [S10][S16]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium. **Reserve life**: proved reserves of 32.3 Mt at end-2025 [S16] and 62.6 Mt on [S8]'s undated mineable statement [S8] are a small number of years at the plan rate, and the mine needs the exploration programme to convert the 147 Mt resource [S8][S12]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high. **FX and pricing**: BSSR reports in US dollars but pays costs in rupiah and is priced in rupiah, so the rupiah path moves the translated value [S0]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium. **Governance and liquidity**: the free float is very small and the controlling shareholder holds the overwhelming majority [S0], so the shares are illiquid and minority influence is limited. Likelihood: known. Impact: medium. **Cost run-rate**: we carry the first-half operating-cost rate, which earned a 37.4% gross margin and a US$79.7m operating profit [S2]; the risk is that the half's stripping and mix were favourable and costs revert towards the FY2025 ratio, which would take our profit down rather than the reverse. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium.

We mirror the scenarios on the same three drivers — the marker price, sales volume and the payout — with base probability at half. Bear (25%): the war premium fades and China restarts idled mines, so the marker prices a fifth below the deck and low-calorie tonnes take the first hit; the reserve-conversion programme stalls, so the mine can schedule only the 32.3 Mt proved reserve across the DCF rather than the 147 Mt resource; and the payout is cut as profit falls, giving Rp2,425 [S16][S8]. Bull (25%): the premium persists and Indonesian supply discipline holds, so the marker prices a fifth above the deck, volumes rise modestly and the payout is held at the top of the observed range, giving Rp6,934. Base (50%): Rp5,192. The royalty is carried at the base rate in every scenario because no schedule governs a coal contract of work and the contract rate is unconfirmed [S19].

The bull is incomplete on the upside by construction: exploration beyond the 147 Mt measured resource is a free option that requires a sourced conversion schedule, and we do not capitalise it [S12][S16]. That is a deliberate omission, not a neutral assumption, and it is the first thing a long-only reader should press us on. The dividend cut the bear carries matters because the expected return leans on the next-twelve-month DPS, so a normalising payout is a first-order risk to the return, not a footnote.

Signposts that would change the view: the confirmed contract royalty rate; the FY2026 reserve statement; the FY2027 RKAB volume; the second-half gross margin against the first half's 37.4%; and a decisive move in the Newcastle marker away from US$105/t.

Ownership is concentrated: the controlling shareholder, PT Wahana Sentosa Cemerlang, holds the overwhelming majority of the shares and the free float is under a tenth [S0]. That is a classic IDX structure risk of thin float, limited minority voice, and a controlling party able to shape distribution policy, which it has used: the FY2025 dividend was US$125.0m against parent profit of US$84.0m [S11]. The board combines executive and independent commissioners, and the FY2024 accounts were audited with an unqualified opinion [S9]. We found no pledged-share disclosure, no related-party flow of note and no special-notation or monitoring-board status in the archived record; that is a "none found, checked" statement, not a clean bill [S0][S9].

The dividend record is the clearest signal of how the controlling party uses the company: BSSR has paid out at or above earnings for several years, declared US$125.0m for FY2025 against parent profit of US$84.0m [S11], paid a final dividend for the prior year after the balance-sheet date [S11], and moved again with a US$60.0m interim for the current year [S7]. That is shareholder-friendly while the cash is there, but it also means less is retained against the reserve-conversion programme, so the payout and the mine life compete for the same dollars [S12].

ESG exposures are the sector's standard ones: the emissions from the coal itself, methane and mine-site rehabilitation, with mining in Kalimantan where the sector's environmental record is closely watched [S8][S16]. Financing and reputational pressure on thermal coal is a structural headwind rather than a near-term cash-flow risk at current pricing. On governance, the combination of a very thin float, an overwhelming controlling stake and a distribution policy set by that controller is the structure to watch; we found no evidence of the sharper IDX governance flags — pledged controlling shares, serial rights issues or an auditor downgrade — but the structure is inherently minority-unfriendly [S0][S9].

Dated catalysts: the Q3 2026 results and FY2027 volume plan [S16]; the 2027 RKAB production approval [S10]; and the FY2026 annual report, which should settle the reserve and contract-rate questions [S16]. Between updates we monitor the Newcastle marker against the deck's through-cycle level US$105/t [S0]; monthly volumes and the export mix, particularly the China and India split [S16]; the realised price against our calibrated ratio 31.8% [S0]; the royalty rate actually paid [S0]; the dividend declared against earnings [S11]; the second-half gross margin against the first half's 37.4% [S2]; and progress on the exploration programme that underwrites reserve conversion [S12]. The single most useful number to watch is the realised price against the deck marker, because BSSR's discount to Newcastle is the one variable in the model that is calibrated rather than sourced and could move either way; the second is the royalty rate actually paid, which settles the licence question that dominates our risk list [S0][S16].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: CONVERSION FAILURE, the risk the report names. The war premium fades and China restarts idled mines, so the Newcastle marker prices 20% below the deck and BSSR's low-calorie tonnes take the first hit; the reserve-conversion programme stalls, so the mine can schedule only its 32.3 Mt proved reserve at 31 Dec 2025 (F5/S16) across the ten-year DCF — 3.23 Mt a year, 0.193x the plan — instead of the 147 Mt measured resource; and the payout is cut to ~0.62 as profit falls. The royalty is carried at the base rate in every scenario because the contract rate is unconfirmed and no schedule governs a PKP2B (C7 accepted). The volume asymmetry with the bull is sourced by the proved-resource statement.

bull.narrative: The war premium persists and Indonesian supply discipline holds, so the marker prices 20% above the deck and BSSR lifts volumes 5% above plan with the extra tonnes going to India and China, which takes the mine to the full 147 Mt measured resource well before the ten-year horizon (the model's reserve stock caps it there); and the payout is held at the top of the observed range (payout ~1.28) as dividend capacity persists. The royalty is carried at the base contract rate: the plain-IUP 0.115 band is not reachable for a PKP2B holder and is removed (C7). The exploration upside beyond the 147 Mt measured resource (blocks 5/6/7, S12) is not capitalised — it is a free option requiring a sourced conversion schedule, so the bull is incomplete on the upside by construction.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs benchmark price and IDR/USD
12-month value vs volume and unit cost intensity

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: ANCHORED ON THE COMPANY'S FY2026 PLAN, CONVERTED FROM PRODUCTION TO SALES. BSSR targets 17 Mt of production for FY2026 (F9/S16, split 11 Mt AGM and 6 Mt own mine) after deliberately cutting output in FY2025 to 17.843 Mt production and 17.579 Mt sales (F4/F2/S16) against 21.35 Mt production and 20.79 Mt sales in FY2024 (F3/F1/S9). Sales ran at 98.5% of production in FY2025 and 97.4% in FY2024, so the 17 Mt production target is carried at 16.75 Mt of sales (17.0 x 0.9852, F2/F4); the red team was right that the model had used production as sales. Management said the FY2025 cut was a price-defence decision, and the reduction 'berbuah manis' with a stronger Q1 2026 (S16). No sourced driver supports a further decline, so the plan rate is held flat until the 147 Mt measured resource is exhausted; the trough case is carried in the bear.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025A revenue of US$703.77m (S0) over FY2025A sales of 17.579 Mt (F2/S16) gives an ASP of ~US$40.0/t; the coal deck's FY2025A Newcastle average is US$108.4/t (deck.coal.newc.FY2025A, World Bank Pink Sheet), so the realised ratio to the benchmark that prices this name is 0.369. The ratio is held flat across the forecast — NOT fitted to the deck's FY2026E Newcastle spike of 137.0 (a war-premium print the desk expects to mean-revert); a ratio fitted to the spike would carry a trough realised price into the long run. BSSR realises a deep discount to Newcastle because its product is a low-calorie thermal coal (its own marketing runs a large domestic share — Indonesia ~30% of the FY2025 mix — and its exports go to India and China, S8/S16), and the deck's ICI-4/ICI-3 series that would price 4,200-5,000 kcal coal are needs_source, so the reviewed Newcastle deck is the pricing benchmark and HBA is used only for the royalty band and the DMO cap. FY2026 IS DELIBERATELY ANCHORED TO THE THROUGH-CYCLE MARKER, not the deck's FY2026 war print: the 1H2026 actual revenue of US$361.1m (F11/S2) annualises to ~US$722m, whereas the deck's FY2026E marker of 137.0 applied at the structural 0.369 gives ~US$847m and implies a 2H realisation above today's spot. The red team's C8 was right. FY2026 therefore carries realisation 0.3178, which prices the same year at the deck's FY2027E marker of 118.0 (118.0 x 0.369 / 137.0 = 0.3178) and lands revenue at ~US$729m, ~1% above the 1H annualisation; from FY2027 the structural 0.369 is restored as the benchmark falls to 118.0, so the ASP path is flat rather than a spike and a trough. The calibration flag this creates is an artifact of pricing a 2026 year at 2025 volumes and is justified in qc_justifications.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: BSSR's own mine and AGM sell to the domestic market as well as export (Indonesia ~30% of the FY2025 mix, S16), and domestic power tonnage sits under the standing US$70/t DMO cap carried in the coal deck (d.coal.dmo_cap). At the calibrated realisation of ~US$40/t the cap does not bind, so the assumption is disclosure rather than a value driver.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads as cost-intensity (units of cash cost per tonne), because no archived source in this window discloses BSSR's actual strip ratio. cost_per_bcm is therefore the mining cash cost per tonne (S0/S9).

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Backed out of the FY2025 accounts with the RESTATED D&A so the model reproduces the FY2025A result: FY2025A cost of revenue of US$495.18m (S0) over 17.579 Mt of sales, less the royalty at the stated base rate (0.1475 of revenue = US$103.81m) and the restated D&A of US$61.72m (F18), leaves a cash cost ex-royalty of US$329.65m, or US$18.75/t at an intensity of 1.0. The red team was right that the old US$22.26/t plug absorbed the missing D&A: the pair is fixed by total cost of revenue, so the split now carries the true cash cost and the true non-cash charge rather than understating both EBITDA and the FCFF add-back. FY2026E IS SET SO THE FUEL PASS-THROUGH IS PRICED AT THE THROUGH-CYCLE BRENT, not the deck's FY2026E war print (QC Q2): the template multiplies every year by (1 + fuel_share x (brent_t / brent_FY2025A - 1)), and brent FY2026E of 96.0 against the FY2025A 68.1 would add ~2.3/t of diesel cost to the same year whose coal revenue is deliberately priced at the FY2027E through-cycle marker (C8). Setting FY2026E cost_per_bcm to 17.870 makes the post-pass-through FY2026E unit cost 20.07/t, exactly the FY2027E unit cost computed from the base 18.753/t at the same FY2027E through-cycle brent of 84.0 (18.753 x 1.0700 = 20.07), so the war premium is rejected on the cost side exactly as it is on the revenue side. From FY2027E the base 18.753/t is held in real terms and escalated with the deck.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried in cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the two lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling and barging cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK (S0).

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: RESTATED FROM THE REPORTED EBITDA MARGIN. The red team's FATAL was correct: S16 states the FY2025 EBITDA margin was 23.31% (F17), which on US$703.77m revenue (S0) is US$164.05m of EBITDA, against US$102.33m of reported EBIT (S0) — an implied D&A of US$61.72m (F18), or US$3.51/t on 17.579 Mt. The data pack's US$0.125m is a residual, not the charge. The PPE roll-forward corroborates the computed figure independently: US$143.95m opening PPE plus US$33.89m capex less US$117.03m closing PPE is US$60.81m of depreciation in FY2025 (S0). A full-text grep of every registered source finds no penyusutan/depresiasi/depreciation line (the FY2025 audited LK is not archived; bssr.co.id is unreachable and IDX is refused by design), so the margin-implied figure is the best available and is disclosed as computed. The forecast holds the same US$3.51/t charge flat; the FCFF now adds back the full charge, not only its tax shield.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the company's FY2026 capex budget of US$26.3m (F10/S16) over the 17 Mt plan = ~US$1.55/t; FY2025 actual capex was US$33.9m (S0). Held flat in real terms.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE 1H2026 ACTUAL, not the FY2025 ratio (QC Q5). The first half of 2026 earned an operating profit of US$79.7m (F21/S2) on US$361.1m of revenue (F11/S2) and the pack's quarterly opex lines sum to US$49.82m (2026Q1 US$24.24m plus 2026Q2 US$25.58m, S0) — 13.80% of revenue, against 15.1% for FY2025. The company's own commentary is that operating expense "tumbuh lebih lambat" (grew more slowly) than revenue (S2). The 1H2026 dollar opex of US$49.8m annualises to US$99.6m, below the FY2025 US$106.3m, so holding the 1H2026 ratio carries the observed cost improvement rather than assuming a second-half step-down with no source. The same ratio is held across the forecast.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ANCHORED ON THE LAST ACTUAL DISTRIBUTION, with FY2026E adjusted for dividend TIMING (QC Q3). BSSR declared US$125m against US$83.98m of parent profit for FY2025 — 148.8% (F8/F7/S11, and F15 restates dps so the engine's payout_ratio equals the sourced 148.8%) — and the FY2025 pack FCF of US$127.7m (OCF US$161.62m less capex US$33.89m, S0) covered it. The evidence since the balance-sheet date points the same way: the FY2026 interim dividend of US$60m (F19/S7) is 95% of 1H2026 net profit of US$63.0m (F12/S2), so 0.95 is the policy payout from FY2027E. FY2026E is set to 0.3395, a TIMING input rather than a policy change: the US$60m interim was declared 17 September 2026 and PAID 9 October 2026 (F19/S7), before this valuation date, so the cash a buyer at today's price still receives inside twelve months is the FY2026 final tranche only — the engine's dps line (and therefore val.dps12) is the residual (0.95 x US$98.3m FY2026E net profit less the US$60m interim = US$33.4m), while the interim is deducted once in the valuation bridge. The bear cuts the policy payout to ~0.62; the bull holds the top of the observed range at ~1.28. The market values IDX coal on dividend capacity (method card 5).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0 for cross-name consistency (every COAL sibling carries terminal_growth 0.0 and the life-DCF primary carries no terminal value, so no method consumes this input).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: diesel is ~30% of the mining cost stack (S0)

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 operating working capital of US$71.37m over US$703.77m revenue is 10.14% (S0), and the ratio has risen every year (1.4% FY2023, 5.1% FY2024, 10.1% FY2025), so the 3-year average of 5.54% was an unjustified optimism that booked a one-time working-capital release. The red team was right; the forecast now holds the last actual, so FY2026 carries a working-capital build rather than a release. The model charges the increment against FCFF each year.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; expansion sits inside the FY2026 capex budget reflected in capex_unit

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: THE CONTRACT RATE IS UNCONFIRMED, but the LICENCE CLASS IS NOT: AGM holds a PKP2B [S19], whose PNBP is contract-specific (PP 15/2022 Art. 14(2); the deck's coal.royalty_pkp2b is needs_source), so no archive-backed contract rate exists and the rate is a stated base rather than a read one. The base carries 0.1475, the mid-point of the two schedule values reachable at our HBA path: the ex-PKP2B IUPK band 0.18 (deck coal.royalty_iupk at HBA 70-120, where d.coal.hba 105-118 sits) and the plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band 0.115 (deck coal.royalty_iup_mid at HBA>=90). The scenarios price those two ends directly (+/-0.0325). The unreachable 0.27 (an HBA>=160 band) and the unpinned 0.09 (the <=4,200 kcal tranche) are removed. Confirm the contract rate from the FY2026 annual report.

challenges.challenge: FY2025 EBITDA is understated by ~60%. S16 — the report's own source for volume, capex and reserves — states "Margin EBITDA berada di level 23,31% pada 2025", i.e. 0.2331 x $703.77m = $164.05m. The model carries $102.46m (14.6%). The $61.7m gap is exactly the D&A the report admits the pack understates ($0.125m, a ~900-year asset life on $117.0m PPE). Because the pack's opex line ($106.3m) must include that D&A for the company's margin to reconcile, the model's EBITDA = EBIT + D&A is effectively EBIT, and the forecast FCFF adds back only 0.688/t ($11.7m) instead of the ~61.7m implied. The report's claim that the FCFF effect is "the tax shield only and second-order (about US$3m/yr)" is wrong: the missing add-back is ~$50m/yr, roughly $300m of PV and about a doubling of the $305.8m DCF enterprise value. The same error carries the 25%-weight EV/EBITDA leg: 5.27x on $102.5m gives 4,473, while 5.27x on $164.0m gives ~Rp6,700. Net profit, tax and ROE (S16 30.76%) are consistent, so this is isolated to EBITDA/D&A — but it is dispositive for the target and the REDUCE rating.
challenges.answer: Accepted. S16's 23.31% FY2025 EBITDA margin is verbatim; at US$703.77m revenue it implies US$164.05m EBITDA against US$102.33m EBIT, so D&A is US$61.72m (US$3.51/t), corroborated by the PPE roll-forward (143.95 + 33.89 - 117.03 = 60.81). The pack's US$0.125m is a residual. FY2025A D&A is restated as computed fact F18; cost of revenue is split into cash cost 18.753/t and D&A 3.5109/t with total cogs unchanged, so EBIT is unchanged and EBITDA rises to 164.05. The forecast adds back the full charge. Calibration before the FY2026 price anchor matched at -0.27%.

challenges.challenge: The DCF discounts 10 years x 17 Mt = 170 Mt, which exceeds the 147 Mt measured resource (S8) by 23 Mt, is 2.7x the 62.6 Mt mineable proved reserves (S8) and 5.3x the 32.3 Mt end-2025 reserves (S16). The report discloses the conflict and calls the resource "the floor", but 170 Mt is above that floor and the horizon is fixed at 10 years in every scenario. The method card says reserves plus high-confidence resources only, with exploration a free option never in base NAV; the 23 Mt beyond the measured resource is exactly that option. The 62.6 Mt "mineable" figure is the appropriate DCF base (≈3.7 years at plan), yet the report uses the lower 32.3 Mt only for the disclosure and the higher 147 Mt for the valuation — a one-way anchor choice.
challenges.answer: Accepted. F6's key is changed from resource to reserves, so the template's depleting stock is the 147 Mt measured resource; the DCF now mines it and stops (volume 13.0 Mt in FY2034E, zero in FY2035E) instead of discounting 170 Mt. The reserve ladder is disclosed: 32.3 Mt proved at 31 Dec 2025 (F5/S16) is the bear's conversion-failure case, 62.6 Mt mineable proved (F16/S8, undated) sits between, and 147 Mt measured (F6/S8) is the base stock. Nothing beyond the measured resource is capitalised; exploration is disclosed as an uncapitalised option.

challenges.challenge: The bear does not price reserve exhaustion or conversion failure. Its four shocks are newc x0.8, volume x0.95, royalty +0.0325 and payout x0.65; the DCF still runs 10 years / 170 Mt. With 32.3 Mt proved at end-2025 (S16) the mine has ~1.9 years at the 17 Mt plan; a bear that cuts the horizon to the proved life or assumes no resource conversion is far more damaging than a 5% volume slip. §4 says "a stalled conversion is what the bear prices", but the bear contains no such shock — the stated hedge does not exist.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear now shocks a.volume x0.193, which schedules only the 32.3 Mt proved reserve (F5/S16) across the ten-year DCF (3.23 Mt a year), and the narrative names conversion failure. The out-of-band multiplier and the volume asymmetry are justified in qc_justifications with the proved-reserve source. Bear value is Rp3,388.

challenges.challenge: The bull does not capitalise the exploration / reserve-conversion upside. The company is drilling blocks 5, 6 and 7 to convert the 147 Mt measured resource (S12/S16) and the report calls exploration "a first-order input to the value", but the bull only shocks marker +20%, volume +5%, royalty -0.0325 and payout x1.35. A successful conversion extends the mine beyond the 10-year DCF, yet no life-extension, resource-conversion or terminal-value leg exists in the bull. The 10-year DCF with zero terminal value deliberately excludes what the company is spending to create.
challenges.answer: Accepted as a disclosure, not a valuation change. The bull does not capitalise exploration beyond the 147 Mt measured resource; the narrative now states the bull is incomplete on the upside by construction and that the omission is deliberate, not neutral. No sourced conversion schedule exists to value the option, so it is not booked.

challenges.challenge: The base payout of 0.70 is less than half the FY2025 actual 1.49 (F8/F7) and below the 5-year average, and the "run-off, cannot persist" claim is contradicted by the pack's own cash flow: FY2025 FCF was $127.7m (S0: OCF $161.6m less capex $33.9m) against $125m of declared dividends, so the payout was cash-covered. The report instead cites "free cash flow of US$25.4m" — the model's FCFF, not FCF — and says it "ran above net profit of US$84.0m", which is arithmetically false (25.4 < 84.0). On the actual FCF, the dividend is fundable. The expected return uses a next-12m DPS of Rp626, less than half the pack's dps_ttm of Rp1,242; at Rp866 (FY2025's Rp125m) the return is -5.4%, not -10.2%, and at the trailing Rp1,242 it is +2.9% (HOLD). The rating is sensitive to a payout assumption that is below the last actual and not sourced.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The false 'FCF 25.4 above NP 84.0' sentence is removed. The pack's operating cash flow less capex covered the US$125m declared dividend in FY2025 (S0), and the base payout is raised to 0.95, sourced to the FY2026 interim of US$60m = 95% of 1H2026 net profit of US$63m (F19/S7, F12/S2). The model's FCFF is disclosed as lower only because it charges a working-capital build.

challenges.challenge: The dividend cross-check capitalises a finite-life dividend as a perpetuity at a 10.9% cap rate (average of the peer median 6.95% and the own 5-year 14.92%), producing Rp5,728 — 101% above the DCF and 15% of the blend. For a depleting asset with 32.3 Mt proved (~2 years) the dividend cannot be perpetual, and the pack's own dps_ttm of Rp1,242 at Rp5,000 implies a 24.8% current yield, more than double the cap rate used. The report says the cap rate, not a peak payout, flatters the leg; that is the defect: it applies a no-depletion perpetuity to a mine with a short reserve life and uses a cap rate the market is not using.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The dividend-capitalisation leg is dropped from the blend (weight 0.0) because a no-depletion perpetuity at a 10.9% cap rate is the wrong treatment for a depleting mine. The dividend is retained only in the total return (next-12m DPS Rp515) and as a prose cross-check. DCF/EV-EBITDA weights renormalise to 0.65/0.35.

challenges.challenge: The bull's royalty endpoint of 0.115 (plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band) is not a regime a PKP2B holder can reach. The report's own §2 says a contract of work's PNBP follows the individual contract and "the banded calorie-by-HBA open-pit schedules do not govern it"; the deck's ex-PKP2B continuation list (KPC, Arutmin, Berau, MHU, Kendilo, AADI) maps to the IUPK 0.18 band, which the bear already uses. The bull narrative ("the contract is reconstituted on the plain-IUP mid-calorie open-pit band") is therefore an unsourced regime change, and it is the bull's "single largest value read" lifting the 25%-weight bull (6,736) and the weighted target (3,863). If the bull must stay inside the PKP2B class, its royalty is the contract rate or the IUPK continuation band, and the bull and target fall.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The plain-IUP 0.115 royalty shock is removed from the bull; the royalty is carried at the base contract rate in every scenario because no schedule governs a PKP2B and the contract rate is unconfirmed. The ex-PKP2B IUPK 0.18 continuation band is disclosed as the downside bound only.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of $859.4m is 19% above the 1H2026 annualised run-rate ($722.2m from $361.1m, F11/S2), and the implied 2H2026 realisation (~$59-61/t at flat volume, Newcastle ~$159-169) sits above today's spot of $150.35 and above the deck's own FY2027E of $118.0. The report acknowledges the 1H annualisation but keeps the higher full-year deck marker. With the year ten months done, the base case should be re-anchored to the 1H actual plus the 2H forward curve, not the full-year marker; the FY2026E EBITDA of $177.9m is 74% above the FY2025A $102.5m (and, after C1, the comparison changes again).
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2026 is re-anchored to the 1H2026 actual: realisation 0.3178 prices the year at the deck's FY2027E through-cycle marker of 118.0 (118.0 x 0.369 / 137.0), giving revenue of US$729.3m, about 1% above the 1H annualisation of US$722.2m. The structural 0.369 is restored from FY2027 as the benchmark falls to 118.0, so the ASP path is flat. The calibration and drift flags this creates are justified in qc_justifications.

challenges.challenge: The base royalty of 14.75% is a constructed midpoint of the two scenario bands (0.18 and 0.115), not the contract rate or the LK's effective rate. The report says the contract rate is unconfirmed, which is honest, but the cost plug is backed out so that FY2025A EBITDA is unchanged whatever rate is chosen ("the plug moves with the stated royalty rate"). The calibration therefore cannot test the royalty, and the base is neither the contract nor an observed rate. The FY2025 LK's royalty expense (or the PP 15/2022 contract schedule) would settle it; the report says the LK is unavailable but does not show that the royalty line was searched for in the archive.
challenges.answer: Accepted that the base is not an observed rate; rebutted that one is available. A full-text search of every registered source finds no royalty or PNBP line for BSSR, and the FY2025 LK is not archived (company site unreachable, IDX refused). The base therefore remains a stated unconfirmed 0.1475, now disclosed as the midpoint of the two schedule values reachable at our HBA path, with the search stated in the report and the sensitivity shown. The cost plug no longer holds EBITDA constant: D&A is restated independently from S16, so the royalty is not absorbing the D&A gap.

challenges.challenge: Unjustified optimism in working capital. The model's nwc_pct of 5.54% is the 3-year average, but the last actual is 10.14% ($71.4m / $703.8m) and rising (1.4% -> 5.1% -> 10.1%). The FY2026E FCFF includes a $23.8m one-time working-capital release; holding nwc at the last actual would be a ~$15.7m use, a ~$39.5m FCFF swing (~Rp270/share). No source justifies normalising below the last actual.
challenges.answer: Accepted. nwc_pct is held at the last actual 10.14% (US$71.4m / US$703.8m) rather than the 5.54% three-year average, so FY2026 carries a working-capital build rather than a release.

challenges.challenge: The reserve reconciliation characterises S8's 62.6 Mt as "an earlier 'mineable' (post-dilution) basis" and S16's 32.3 Mt as "the later end-2025 audited-class number", but S8 carries no as-of date and no basis statement (verified snippet: "a measured resource of 147 million tonnes, and 62.6 million tonnes of mineable proved reserves"). The "earlier" reading is an inference presented as fact, and the two statements remain unreconciled.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 'earlier/later' chronology is removed. S8's 62.6 Mt is presented as undated with no basis statement, S16's 32.3 Mt is dated 31 December 2025, and the two are shown as conflicting rather than reconciled by inference.

challenges.challenge: The model uses the 17 Mt FY2026 production target as sales volume, but FY2025 sales were 98.5% of production (17.579 / 17.843, F2/F4). At the same ratio, 17 Mt of production implies ~16.75 Mt of sales, so the model's volume is ~1.5% high (and the per-tonne cost/D&A denominators move with it).
challenges.answer: Accepted. Volume is 16.75 Mt of sales, the 17 Mt FY2026 production target (F9/S16) converted at the FY2025 sales/production ratio of 98.52% (F2/F4). The per-tonne cost and D&A denominators use the same 16.75 Mt.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull shocks only the marker, volume, royalty band and payout; it does not capitalise the 147 Mt resource conversion / life extension the report calls a first-order value input (C4), nor hold the last actual 1.49 payout or the 24.8% trailing dividend yield (C5).

missing_bear_case.note: The bear has no reserve-exhaustion or conversion-failure shock: 32.3 Mt proved is ~2 years at the 17 Mt plan, yet the DCF still runs 10 years / 170 Mt in every scenario, despite §4 saying "a stalled conversion is what the bear prices" (C2, C3).

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E revenue of $859.4m sits 19% above the annualised 1H2026 actual ($722.2m) and implies a 2H realisation above today's spot; nwc is normalised below the last actual; the royalty base is a constructed midpoint rather than the contract or LK rate (C8, C9, C10).

evidence_and_citations.note: F1/F3/F7/F8 verify in S9/S11 and F2/F5/F9/F10 in S16, but the report's FY2025 EBITDA ($102.5m, 14.6%) contradicts its own S16 quote (23.31% margin ≈ $164m); "free cash flow $25.4m ran above net profit $84.0m" is arithmetically false (25.4 < 84.0); S8's reserve date/basis is inferred (C1, C5, C11).

valuation_method_fit.note: Right primary method and a clean net-debt/minority bridge, but the 10-year / 170 Mt DCF exceeds the 147 Mt measured resource and 2.7x the 62.6 Mt mineable proved reserves; the dividend leg is a no-depletion perpetuity; the disclosed reserve conflict is not transmitted into the valuation (C2, C6).

bias_and_tone.note: Disclosure is strong and the royalty is now bracketed, but the prose leans one way: the "run-off payout" is asserted while FY2025 FCF ($127.7m) covered the $125m dividend; the bull royalty endpoint is a schedule that does not govern a PKP2B; the "second-order (~$3m/yr)" D&A claim is wrong (C1, C5, C7).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads d.coal.newc / HBA / DMO / brent and the PKP2B class consistently, but the bull's 0.115 is the plain-IUP band while the deck's ex-PKP2B continuation list maps to IUPK 0.18; the FY2026E marker (137.0) is above the deck's own FY2027E (118.0) and spot (150.35) on a 2H basis (C7, C8).

bias.note: Both round-1 defects are corrected and verified. The bridge now deducts the FY2025 final of US$70m (RUPST 15 June, paid 8 July, so a current liability at the 30 June balance sheet) and the FY2026 interim of US$60m (approved 17 September, paid 9 October) once each [S11/S7], which is the right walk-forward from 30 June net cash to the 4 November valuation date. findings.finding: The FY2026 price anchor is carried in a.realisation (0.3178 against the calibrated 0.369) rather than in the benchmark. The resulting ASP (about US$43.5/t) is right and matches the 1H2026 run-rate, but the encoding leaves calibration.ebitda at -27.7% and drift.realisation at +16% even though the year is correctly priced. The gates no longer test the cost and volume of the first forecast year, which is the check they exist to perform.

params_basis and royalty_rate.basis still describe royalty scenario shocks that the live scenarios no longer carry: they say the bear prices 0.18 and the bull 0.115, mirrored at +/-0.0325, while the actual bear and bull shocks are the marker, volume and payout only and the plain-IUP 0.115 bull band was removed under C7. Stale text contradicts the scenario record and would mislead the next reader of fund record.

The PKP2B contract rate remains unconfirmed. The 0.1475 base is the midpoint of two reachable schedule bands, not an observed contract or FY2025 LK rate, and the calibration cannot test it. The licence class is sourced [S19] and the rate is carried at the base in every scenario, consistent with the C7 fix.

Consensus quarantine clean. One consensus sentence was stripped at ingest from each of S2-S6 and S9 and none from S7/S8, and no broker estimate, target price or consensus number enters the model or the prose; every input traces to a company announcement, the FY2025 accounts in the pack, or a house deck.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 118.6 vs the actual 164.0 (-28%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: the FY2026E realisation of 0.3178 is a deliberate one-year price anchor to the deck's FY2027E through-cycle marker of 118.0, taken because the 1H2026 actual revenue of US$361.1m annualises to about US$722m against the ~US$847m the deck's FY2026E war print implies [S2/F11]. The calibration re-prices FY2025 at FY2025 volumes and benchmark, so a 2026 price anchor mechanically fails it; the cost base is the FY2025 actual (18.753/t at the FY2025 fuel price) with FY2026E cost_per_bcm set to 17.870 only so the through-cycle-brent pass-through reconciles to that same 20.07/t unit cost [S0/F18], and the FY2025 history still reconciles at the 23.31% reported EBITDA margin [S16/F17].

flags.message: a.realisation moves +16% from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: the +16% from FY2026E to FY2035E is a one-year step back to the structural 0.369, not a trend: FY2026 is deliberately priced at the deck's FY2027E through-cycle marker (118.0) because the 1H2026 actual revenue of US$361.1m annualises to about US$722m, not the ~US$847m the deck's FY2026E war print implies [S2/F11]. The benchmark itself falls from 137.0 to 118.0, so the realised ASP path is flat (about US$43.5/t in both years) rather than a spike followed by a trough.

flags.message: a.payout moves +61.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: the FY2026E payout input is a dividend-TIMING adjustment, not a policy change (QC Q3): the US$60m FY2026 interim was declared 17 September 2026 and paid 9 October 2026 [S7/F19], before the 4 November 2026 valuation date, so the engine's FY2026E dps line is the residual final tranche only and the interim sits once in the valuation bridge; FY2027E onward returns to the 0.95 record payout that the 1H2026 interim itself evidences (US$60m against US$63m of first-half net profit) [S2/F12].

flags.message: the bear case multiplies a.volume by 0.193 (outside 0.5-2.0)
flags.justification: the bear's volume multiplier of 0.193 is deliberately outside the 0.5 bound because it is not a demand shock: it steps the mine down to the proved-reserve rate. 32.3 Mt of proved reserves at 31 Dec 2025 [S16/F5] spread across the ten-year DCF is 3.23 Mt a year, 0.193x the 16.75 Mt plan; the conversion-failure case the report names cannot be expressed inside a +/-5% demand band.

flags.message: a.volume: bear 0.193 vs bull 1.05 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: the volume shocks are intentionally asymmetric: the bear schedules only the 32.3 Mt proved reserve [S16/F5] over the ten-year DCF (0.193x), while the bull lifts the plan 5% and hits the 147 Mt measured-resource cap [S8/F6] before the horizon ends. The asymmetry is the reserve question, and the source for it is the two reserve statements, not a symmetric demand band.

flags.message: PKP2B royalty is contract-specific: set a.royalty_rate to the rate the contract or LK shows and justify it with that source
flags.justification: flat mode is used because the licence class is PKP2B [S19]: AGM is stated to hold a PKP2B contract, so the PNBP follows the individual contract (PP 15/2022 Art. 14(2)) and the deck's PKP2B schedule is contract-specific (coal.royalty_pkp2b needs_source, which warns that the IUPK ex-PKP2B schedule must not be substituted). The contract rate is not archived — a full-text search of every registered source finds no royalty/PNBP line for BSSR [S2-S21] — so a.royalty_rate is a stated unconfirmed rate (0.1475), disclosed as such. The plain-IUP 0.115 band is not reachable for a PKP2B and is no longer used in any scenario (C7); the 0.18 ex-PKP2B IUPK continuation band is disclosed as the downside bound in §2 and §5.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'div_yield': 0.15}
flags.justification: the dividend-capacity leg is dropped from the blend (weight 0) because a no-depletion perpetuity at a 10.9% cap rate is the wrong treatment for a depleting mine with 32.3 Mt of proved reserves [S16/F5]; the DCF and EV/EBITDA weights are renormalised to 0.65/0.35 and the dividend cross-check is shown in prose without a weight (C6).
